analysis.title: Cross Asset Hedging: Broader risks call for smarter hedges
key_insights: Credit recorded the largest increase in volatility across asset classes over the month, pushing the average cost of tail hedging in credit to the 34th 18y percentile from the 6th percentile last month.
Rates vol also rose on uncertainty over the growth-inflation mix and monetary policy. Equity vol rose modestly. FX and commodity vols were the only asset classes to decline over the month.

Overall cross-asset tail hedging cost/benefit rose to the 37th 18y percentile this month. Percentiles by asset class: Credit 47th, FX 58th, Rates 34th, Commodity 8th, Equity 54th (as read from Exhibit 2 labels).
BofA continues to favour selective tail and proxy hedges. FX puts screen cheap, particularly CADUSD and AUDUSD puts. In credit, IG spread and iTraxx Main payers offer the best value.

Equity hedges remain expensive, particularly in AI-heavy indices. Proxy hedging and hybrid structures using cross-asset correlations (e.g. NDX-rates structures) are suggested as a cheaper way to hedge AI-related tail risks.
The cross-asset screen shows the hedges most underpricing historical tail events are CADUSD puts, AUDUSD puts and CDX IG payers.
Credit hedges richened after the vol increase. iTraxx Xover payers and, to a lesser extent, CDX HY payers moved toward the middle of the screen, leaving FX hedges at the top.

Rates and commodity hedges remain relatively expensive with dispersion inside each class. EUR 10Y receivers screen less attractive than US counterparts, and copper and aluminium puts offer better value than crude oil puts.
KOSPI implied volatility declined further over the month, but not enough to make its hedges meaningfully more attractive.
Commodity (BCOM) exposure: puts on CAD-USD, AUD-USD and NZD-USD offer high average hedge benefit and would have outperformed the median hedge in most of the 10 largest BCOM drawdowns.
Global equities (MSCI World): CADUSD puts and XLF puts offer high hedge benefit and would have outperformed the median asset in all the largest drawdowns, except Apr25 for CADUSD.
EM credit (BofA EM Corporate Plus): AUDUSD and CADUSD puts offer high average hedge benefit with relatively contained basis risk.
Diversified multi-asset portfolios (BofA MAST): NZD-USD puts screen strongly and would have outperformed the median hedge in 9 of the top 10 drawdowns, except April 2025.

US equities (S&P 500): XLF puts offer material hedge benefit with limited basis risk and would have outperformed SPX puts in 8 of the 10 largest drawdowns. CDX IG payers offer higher benefit but with significantly greater basis risk.
US small/mid caps (RTY): no proxy offers a positive hedge benefit over RTY puts without significant basis risk.
US tech (NDX): no proxy beats NDX puts without significant basis risk, but XLF puts offer reasonable benefit and would have outperformed NDX puts in 7 of 10 largest drawdowns.
European equities (Euro STOXX 50): SXIP puts would have outperformed SX5E puts in 7 of the 10 largest drawdowns, though every proxy carries basis risk.
UK equities (FTSE 100): SXIP puts would have outperformed FTSE puts in 7 of 10 drawdowns. CDX IG payers give positive benefit but with more basis risk.
Chinese equities (HSCEI) and US HY credit (HYG): no hedges offer a positive hedge benefit over the benchmark puts without significant basis risk.
Japanese equities (Nikkei): CDX IG payers may offer tactical proxy hedging, having outperformed Nikkei puts in 7 of the 10 largest drawdowns.
EM equities (EEM): CADUSD puts offer positive average hedge benefit and outperformed EEM puts in 8 of the 10 largest drawdowns.
Cross-asset correlations have edged lower over the past couple of months but remain above their Apr26 lows. The 3m correlation fell 1.3% since early September and the 12m correlation fell about 0.5%.

Equity vs credit: the S&P 500 gained about 2% over the month while equity vol fell by less than the historical relationship predicts. Euro Stoxx 50 fell about 1% yet its vol declined. European credit spreads widened well beyond the regression estimate.

Macro backdrop: sticky inflation, higher-for-longer rates, tighter financial conditions, and political and fiscal concerns in France, where OAT-Bund spreads are approaching levels last seen in the Eurozone sovereign debt crisis.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CADUSD puts as cross-asset tail and proxy hedge (global equities, EM equities, commodities, EM credit)
trade_ideas.rationale: CADUSD puts are the top of the tail-hedging screen and offer high hedge benefit per unit cost across several benchmarks.
trade_ideas.risk: Basis risk to the benchmark; proxy hedges do not work well for small declines.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AUDUSD puts as cross-asset tail and proxy hedge (EM credit, commodities, multi-asset)
trade_ideas.rationale: AUDUSD puts screen second on the tail hedge screen and rank first for EM credit proxy hedging.

trade_ideas.description: Buy NZDUSD puts to proxy-hedge diversified multi-asset portfolios (BofA MAST)
trade_ideas.rationale: Outperformed the median hedge in 9 of the top 10 MAST drawdowns.
trade_ideas.risk: Did not work in April 2025 drawdown.

trade_ideas.description: Buy CDX IG payers / IG spread and iTraxx Main payers as credit tail hedges
trade_ideas.rationale: Best value within credit and underprice historical tail events.
trade_ideas.risk: Significantly greater basis risk when used as equity proxy.

trade_ideas.description: Buy XLF puts as proxy hedge for US equities (S&P 500), NDX and global equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Outperformed SPX puts in 8 of 10 largest drawdowns and NDX puts in 7 of 10.
trade_ideas.risk: Limited basis risk for S&P 500 but not zero.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SXIP puts as proxy hedge for Euro STOXX 50 and FTSE 100
trade_ideas.rationale: Outperformed SX5E puts in 7 of 10 and FTSE puts in 7 of 10 largest drawdowns.

trade_ideas.description: NDX-rates hybrid structures to hedge AI-related tail risks
trade_ideas.rationale: Cheaper and more efficient than direct equity hedges, which are expensive in AI-heavy indices.

risk_factors: Tighter financial conditions weighing on sentiment and risk appetite, hitting segments that have stayed resilient such as equities
French political and fiscal stress, with OAT-Bund spreads near sovereign debt crisis levels
Basis risk in proxy hedges, which do not often work for small benchmark declines

tension_points.bull_case: Equities have stayed resilient, with the S&P 500 up about 2% over the month and equity vol rising only modestly.
tension_points.bear_case: Tighter financial conditions could weigh on sentiment and risk appetite and pressure segments that have so far held up, while credit vol and spreads are already rising.

theme_stances.key_argument: Broader macro risks favour selective tail and proxy hedges, with FX puts and credit payers screening cheapest and equity hedges expensive.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to favour selective tail and proxy hedges

theme_stances.key_argument: Direct equity hedges are expensive in AI-heavy indices, so proxy and hybrid structures are cheaper ways to hedge AI-related tail risks.
theme_stances.evidence: Equity hedges remain expensive, particularly in AI-heavy indices.
